generator.description: US Naval Observatory API answers for spot checks of the daily almanac pages: Celestial Navigation Data at 4 whole hours, each queried at the ground point of the Sun, the Moon, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn so that body is above the horizon; one-day rise/set/civil twilight at the Greenwich meridian for 6 latitude-dates. Responses verbatim.
generator.never_a_runtime_dependency: Generated by tools/reference/ (Python + Skyfield). CONVENTIONS section 11: never regenerate a fixture from Rust output.

timescale.delta_t_source: Skyfield's bundled skyfield/data/iers.npz, a daily Delta-T table built from the IERS finals2000A.all series at the time the Skyfield wheel was released. Outside the table Skyfield extrapolates with its long-term Delta-T model (Morrison & Stephenson / Espenak & Meeus).
timescale.dut1_definition: DUT1 = UT1 - UTC = 32.184 + Delta_AT - Delta_T, as Skyfield derives it
timescale.leap_second_table: bundled in the same iers.npz; latest offset 37 s from 2017-01-01
timescale.warning_dut1: CONVENTIONS section 6 assumes DUT1 = 0. Skyfield does not: every GHA in these fixtures uses Skyfield's UT1. The per-epoch dut1_s is recorded, and gha_deg_dut1_zero gives the same GHA recomputed with UT1 = UTC so a DUT1 = 0 implementation has a directly comparable number. 1 s of DUT1 = 15.0410686 arcsec of GHA. Beyond the Delta-T table's end the extrapolated Delta-T implies |DUT1| far above the 0.9 s that real leap seconds enforce (about -3.5 s at 2055), so gha_deg alone is not a physically meaningful prediction for far-future epochs; gha_deg_dut1_zero is.

generator.tolerance_justification: The page's precision: 0.1' for GHA and Dec, 1 min for times (USNO rounds to the minute). USNO's Moon runs about 10.36 s late (docs/ACCURACY.md section 7): the Moon is compared at the instant plus 10.36 s, with the same sidereal time.
generator.why_these_instants: Past and present only: for future dates USNO's predicted clock moves the Moon by its motion over tens of seconds (docs/ACCURACY.md section 9).
